articles.title: Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter
articles.read_scope: Complete five-page PDF, including timeout caveats, retry amplification, local quota, periodic jitter, and conclusion.

practice.trigger: A slow dependency produces cascading retries or deployment-only timeouts.
practice.failure: Independent retry layers multiply load; a timeout can occur after a mutation commits.
practice.mechanism: Choose an owning retry layer, cap attempts and elapsed time, jitter delays, and inspect client timeout coverage and retry quota.
practice.conditions: Repeat only operations with a proven duplicate-safe or reconciliation contract; include connection setup and network delay in the budget.
practice.counterexample: A timeout alone neither proves failure nor bounds retry amplification; increasing it can retain scarce resources longer.
practice.verification: Inject dependency slowness, lost responses, cold connections, and recovery; measure downstream attempts, resource occupancy, and committed effects.

articles.limitations: Historical article; installed SDK/version governs retry behavior. Source's broad HTTP error categories need service-specific interpretation.

articles.title: Post mortem on the Cloudflare Control Plane and Analytics Outage
articles.read_scope: Complete article body: intended design, power incident, high availability tests, disaster recovery, bootstrap and remediation.

practice.trigger: A service claims facility resilience or readiness to restore after infrastructure loss.
practice.failure: Component-only tests miss dependencies outside the tested cluster; restored services face accumulated retry traffic.
practice.mechanism: Map the complete failure domain, test its loss, stage bootstrap dependencies, and admit traffic within recovery capacity.
practice.conditions: Use an authorized isolated rehearsal and business-level availability/data-loss criteria.
practice.counterexample: Taking only the highly available portion of a facility offline leaves colocated dependencies available and understates risk.
practice.verification: Demonstrate recovery with the whole declared domain absent, including control tools, logs, configuration, and backlog catch-up.

articles.limitations: Single company's incident. The article labels portions of the facility's electrical sequence as speculation; those claims are not adopted.

articles.title: Terraform 1.1 Improves Refactoring and the Cloud CLI Experience
articles.read_scope: Complete article body, with emphasis on moved statements and the distinction between remote state and remote execution.

practice.trigger: Infrastructure resources are renamed or configuration is reorganized.
practice.failure: An address change can be interpreted as replacement of an existing object.
practice.mechanism: Represent supported same-state address transitions in configuration and review their plan alongside configuration changes.
practice.conditions: Verify Terraform/provider support, resource identity, backend, workspace, and actual plan effects.
practice.counterexample: Renaming a stateful resource is not an ordinary source-code rename; code review alone misses replacement.
practice.verification: Confirm the plan preserves the intended physical objects and rehearse upgrade paths from supported earlier addresses.

articles.limitations: Release announcement explains a historical capability; current docs determine cross-state migration, type compatibility, and migration-history retention.

articles.title: Graceful VM exits, some dials
articles.read_scope: Complete article, including application-specific signal handling and limits introduced by shared proxies.

practice.trigger: A deployment must preserve active connections or work longer than a default stop allowance.
practice.failure: Platform signal, application signal semantics, proxy lifecycle, and drain duration do not agree.
practice.mechanism: Trace the complete stop path and verify current platform limits before choosing finish-in-place or resumable work.
practice.conditions: Signal handling must close admission and retain dependencies needed to complete or checkpoint work.
practice.counterexample: The historical dedicated-VM 24-hour allowance is not the current Machines contract.
practice.verification: Exercise controlled stop and earlier forced interruption, checking business progress rather than process exit alone.

articles.limitations: The page labels 2020-12-29 as its publication date. Historical numeric limits are superseded by current documentation; examples also contain a comment/value mismatch.
